findings.claim: The touch-control button repeats the `.ui-button` type and transition block word for word (this is the clone in clones.md). It also repeats the `.ui-button:active` press sink: same transform, shadow and transition duration. A change to the button type or the press feel has to be made in both files, or the two drift apart.
findings.evidence: components.css:122-131 `.ui-button { … font-family: var(--type-button-font); font-size: var(--type-button-size); font-weight: var(--type-button-weight); font-style: var(--type-button-style); line-height: 1; text-transform: uppercase; … transition: transform var(--duration-release) var(--ease-snap), box-shadow var(--duration-release) var(--ease-snap); }` == touch-controls.css:47-56 (same 10 lines in `.ui-tc`). Press: components.css:134-137 `.ui-button:active { transform: translate(var(--ui-sink-button), var(--ui-sink-button)); box-shadow: var(--ui-shadow-pressed); … transition-duration: var(--duration-press); }` vs touch-controls.css:89-91 `.ui-tc.is-pressed` with the same three declarations. touch-controls.ts:6-7 imports components.css before touch-controls.css.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the copies in components.css. Change the `.ui-button` type and transition declarations into a rule for `.ui-button, .ui-tc` at the same spot, and the press declarations into `.ui-button:active, .ui-tc.is-pressed` (backgrounds stay in their own rules). Then delete the copies from `.ui-tc` and `.ui-tc.is-pressed` in touch-controls.css. Computed styles stay the same: components.css always loads first, and every `.ui-tc` override (--gas type, .is-resting/.is-retracting transition, is-waking animation) comes later with equal or higher specificity. Note that open PR #24 also edits components.css.

findings.claim: The pause card and the results screen each define the same full-width 4:2:1 stripe band (flex 1 / auto width / s3 height, then red flex 4 and mustard flex 2). Only the border-width differs.
findings.evidence: screens.css:115-126 `.ui-pause__stripes .ui-stripe { flex: 1; width: auto; height: var(--space-s3); border-width: var(--outline-default) 0; } .ui-pause__stripes .ui-stripe--red { flex: 4; } .ui-pause__stripes .ui-stripe--mustard { flex: 2; }` vs results.css:28-39 `.ui-results > .ui-stripes .ui-stripe { flex: 1; width: auto; height: var(--space-s3); border-width: 0 0 var(--outline-default); } .ui-results > .ui-stripes .ui-stripe--red { flex: 4; } .ui-results > .ui-stripes .ui-stripe--mustard { flex: 2; }`. results-screen.ts:5-6 imports screens.css before results.css.
findings.suggestedFix: In screens.css, give the three band rules the selector lists `.ui-pause__stripes .ui-stripe, .ui-results > .ui-stripes .ui-stripe` (flex/width/height), plus the matching `--red` and `--mustard` pairs. Keep each screen's own border-width rule, and delete the copies from results.css. Each selector keeps its own specificity, so computed styles don't change. The only rules they compete with are the lower-specificity base `.ui-stripe*` rules.

findings.claim: The minimap stride (every 8th centreline point) is a named constant in the game but a bare `8` in the stage fixture. The fixture's comment says it matches the game, so if the game's stride changes, the stage screenshots quietly stop matching real races.
findings.evidence: game.ts:30 `const MINIMAP_STRIDE = 8;` used at game.ts:251 `world.track.layout.centre.filter((_, i) => i % MINIMAP_STRIDE === 0)`; stage.ts:66-71 `/** … minimap outline (every 8th centreline point, as in the game). */ … outline: centre.filter((_, i) => i % 8 === 0)`.
findings.suggestedFix: Move `MINIMAP_STRIDE` to src/ui/race-ui.ts as an export. Both files already import that module, and it owns the minimap's `reset(outline)`. Use it in game.ts:251 and stage.ts:71.
